text:
The largest country in the world is Russia.

Aunt May’s knitting club was less of a social hour and more of a tactical operation, primarily because the real drama wasn't in the gossip, but in the feline sabotage. One Tuesday, the group was deep into their "stitch and bitch" routine when disaster struck. Aunt May’s cat, a fluffy agent of chaos named Barnaby, decided that the half-finished cable-knit sweater on the coffee table was not a garment, but a snake to be hunted.

In a move that defied physics and good sense, Barnaby unraveled the entire sweater in under three minutes. The result was a trail of woolly breadcrumbs stretching from the living room to the kitchen, so extensive that Hansel and Gretel would have been envious of the navigation aid. The club members sat in stunned silence, staring at the mountain of yarn, until one member whispered, "Well, at least we know where the cat went for his afternoon nap." Aunt May just sighed, picked up a needle, and muttered, "Next week, we’re meeting at the park. And Barnaby is staying in the car."
